questions.q: Which bin color is standard for collecting organic biodegradable wet waste at school?
Painting school building roofs with white reflective paint reduces summer heat due to high surface _____.
How much clean water is wasted in 24 hours by a single leaking tap dripping at 1 drop per second? (Assume 1 drop = 0.05 ml)

Assertion (A): Segregating waste into wet and dry bins at the source protects sanitation workers from injury.
Reason (R): Source segregation prevents broken glass, rusty metal, and hazardous items from getting hidden inside wet organic scraps.
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation.
B) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation.
C) (A) is true, but (R) is false.
D) (A) is false, but (R) is true.
questions.ans: A) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation.

questions.q: Which national initiative mandates clean separate toilets, soap handwashing, and safe water in Indian schools?
questions.scheme: 1 Mark for Swachh Bharat Swachh Vidyalaya.

sections.section_name: Section B: Short Answer & Reasoning (10 Marks)

questions.q: Give Reason: Waste paper and cardboard boxes must be placed in dry waste bins rather than wet food bins.
questions.solution: Wet organic scraps spoil paper fibers with moisture and rot. Keeping paper dry allows traditional recyclers (kabadiwalas) to process and pulp it into recycled paper.
questions.scheme: 1 Mark for wet waste ruining paper fibers; 1 Mark for enabling dry recycling by kabadiwalas.

questions.q: What is a Green School campus? Mention two daily sustainable practices followed in a Green School.
questions.solution: A Green School is an eco-friendly campus prioritizing sustainability. Practices: (1) Source segregation of wet/dry waste, (2) Rainwater harvesting and tap leakage audits.
questions.scheme: 1 Mark for Green School definition; 1 Mark for two daily sustainable practices.

questions.q: Give Reason: White painted building roofs keep classroom interiors cooler during peak summer months.
questions.solution: White paint has a high surface albedo, which reflects incoming shortwave solar radiation back into the atmosphere rather than absorbing thermal heat into the building roof structure.
questions.scheme: 1 Mark for high surface albedo concept; 1 Mark for reflecting solar radiation instead of thermal absorption.

questions.q: How does student-led compost making convert classroom wet waste into a valuable resource for school gardens?
questions.solution: Classroom vegetable peels and food scraps collected in green bins are layered in a compost pit with soil. Microbes decompose organic matter into nutrient-rich humus fertilizer for garden plants.
questions.scheme: 1 Mark for layering organic wet waste in compost pits; 1 Mark for microbial decomposition into natural fertilizer.

questions.q: Calculate the annual water savings if a school fixes 5 dripping taps, each leaking 4 liters of water per day.
questions.solution:
Daily Savings = 5 taps * 4 Liters = 20 Liters per day.
Annual Savings = 20 Liters * 365 days = 7,300 Liters of water saved per year.
questions.scheme: 1 Mark for daily savings calculation (20 L); 1 Mark for annual total calculation (7,300 L).

sections.section_name: Section C: Long Answer, Observation & Application (10 Marks)
sections.question_type: Long Answer / Observation / Diagram / Practical Scenario

questions.q: Design a 3-part Environmental Campus Audit for your school focusing on (a) Water Conservation, (b) Waste Management, and (c) Energy Saving. Outline specific student team audit tasks and actions for each area.
questions.solution:
1. Water Audit Team: Inspect all restroom taps for leaks, measure runoff, install soak pits, and collect rainwater for school gardens.
2. Waste Audit Team: Place color-coded Green (Wet) and Blue (Dry) bins in every classroom, monitor source segregation, and manage leaf composting pits.
3. Energy Audit Team: Ensure lights/fans are switched off during breaks, clean windows for maximum daylight, and advocate white reflective roof coating.
questions.scheme: 1 Mark for overall audit plan structure; 3 Marks for detailed audit tasks across Water, Waste, and Energy (1 Mark each); 1 Mark for practical campus implementation actions.

questions.q: Discuss the crucial role of sanitation workers and traditional recyclers (kabadiwalas) in urban public health. Explain how source waste segregation at school supports their work and prevents landfill environmental pollution.
questions.solution:
1. Role of Sanitation Workers & Kabadiwalas: Sanitation workers keep public spaces clean and collect refuse. Kabadiwalas buy and sort dry recyclables (paper, metal, plastic), diverting tons of material away from municipal landfills.
2. Benefits of Source Segregation:
   - Worker Safety: Separating glass, needles, and sharp metals prevents cut injuries during sorting.
   - Landfill Reduction: Organic wet waste converts to compost, while dry recyclables are processed, drastically reducing landfill pollution.
questions.scheme: 2 Marks for defining civic roles of sanitation workers and recyclers; 2 Marks for safety and recycling benefits of source segregation; 1 Mark for impact on landfill reduction.
